canonical_name: Kolmogorov strong law of large numbers
canonical_statement: On a probability space, if a sequence of real-valued random variables is mutually independent, identically distributed, measurable, and has finite first absolute moment, then its arithmetic means converge almost surely to the common expectation.
domain_and_universes: A measurable probability space (Omega, F, P); X : Nat -> Omega -> Real; proposition in Lean universe 0, with the carrier universe to be fixed during elaboration
hypotheses: the family X is mutually independent
all X n have the same distribution
the common distribution has finite first absolute moment
conclusion: Outside a null set, (1/n) * sum of the first n values X k converges as n tends to infinity to integral of X 0 with respect to P

alternate_encodings.target: centered partial sums divided by n converge almost surely to zero
alternate_encodings.relationship: equivalent after linearity of finite sums and expectation

alternate_encodings.target: distribution-parameterized iid sequence with conclusion at the distribution mean
alternate_encodings.relationship: equivalent once common-law integrability and integral transport are checked

boundary_cases: The average is taken over the first n variables and only its limit as n tends to infinity matters; division at n = 0 and zero-based versus one-based indexing require explicit statement-phase conventions.
excluded_substitutions: weak law or convergence in probability
pairwise independence without an applicable theorem proving sufficiency
finite variance in place of the exact finite-first-moment iid theorem
